name: Cap graft (tip)

card.summary: A small piece of cartilage layered over the nasal tip dome during rhinoplasty to add projection, definition and a smoother tip contour.
card.note: Surgical procedure with risks including warping, extrusion, scarring and donor-site problems; decisions belong with a qualified surgeon.

quick.overview:
A cap graft is a small piece of cartilage placed on top of the nasal tip in rhinoplasty. Surgeons use it to give the tip more definition, projection or a refined shape, which changes the nose's profile and how defined the tip looks from the front and side.

It is described in the Asian rhinoplasty literature as part of the move from silicone implants to cartilage-based tip work, and recent papers describe large and crescent-shaped cap grafts for East Asian patients. A retrospective study of 91 revision patients reported improved satisfaction scores after a modified large-cap graft.
quick.how: A surgeon takes cartilage, commonly from the nasal septum, with ear or rib cartilage used when more is needed, shapes it and fixes it over the tip dome as part of a wider rhinoplasty. This is a hospital or clinic procedure done by a trained plastic or facial surgeon; recovery and swelling can last a year.
quick.risks: In the 91-patient review of a modified large-cap graft, 3.3% had donor-site complications such as pleural tear or hypertrophic scar and 7.7% had recipient-site issues such as warping or extrusion. General rhinoplasty risks include swelling that takes at least a year to settle and shape deformities.

lead: A cap graft is a small piece of cartilage layered on the nasal tip dome during rhinoplasty. It adds definition and projection to the tip and can smooth its contour, so it is used when patients want a more refined or more prominent tip [2][3].

Cartilage for nasal grafts usually comes from the nasal septum. If that is not enough, as in revision surgery, surgeons use cartilage from the ear (concha) or rib [1]. The Asian rhinoplasty literature traces the cap graft as a step in the evolution from dorsum-only implants, through L-shaped implants, to cartilage cap grafts combined with implants and later two-piece augmentation [2].

A retrospective review of 91 East Asian revision patients treated with a modified large-cap graft reported higher outcome scores after surgery, with a 3.3% donor-site complication rate and 7.7% at the recipient site [3]. A 2025 letter describes a crescent-shaped cap graft for Asian noses [4].

chain: Cartilage layered over the tip dome
Tip gains projection and a defined shape
angle.text: The graft physically builds up and reshapes the tip, which can make a short or irregular tip look more defined. Surgeons use it as one element of a larger rhinoplasty plan.

paras: Tip grafts support and reposition the nasal tip. The septal extension graft and columellar strut are the main support grafts discussed in rhinoplasty references, and the cap graft is a different onlay graft for the dome [1][2].

A retrospective study of 91 patients (mean age 26.8) in East Asian revision rhinoplasty used a modified large-cap graft; patient-reported rhinoplasty outcome scores rose from about 11.7 to 17.3 (p<0.001) and blinded surgeons rated contour improvement, with 3.3% donor-site and 7.7% recipient-site complications [3].
A separate paper in a different surgical field used a septal cartilage cap graft for open tracheoplasty in eight patients, and is not about the nasal tip [5].

Reported complications of the modified large-cap graft included pleural tear and hypertrophic scar at the donor site and warping and extrusion at the recipient site [3]. Rhinoplasty references list tip and dorsal deformities such as pollybeak and saddle nose and note that swelling can take at least a year to resolve [1].

timeline.event: Asian rhinoplasty is first described; cap grafts later join the progression of implant techniques [2].
Modified large-cap graft series in East Asian revision rhinoplasty reported [3].
Letter describes a crescent-shaped cap graft technique for Asians [4].
